This podcast series is being launched in conjunction with the 50th anniversary of the American Benefits Council, and today we conclude our interview with former U.S. Representative Earl Pomeroy, while Part 1 covered health care reform and the fallout from the House Republicans' attempt to repeal and replace President Obama's Affordable Care Act. In Part 2, we discussed the process and politics behind comprehensive tax reform, retirement policy challenges, and the rise of state-based benefits legislation. Earl is currently a partner with the law firm of Alston and Byrd and serves on the American Benefits Council's Board of Directors. From 1993 to 2011, he represented the great state of North Dakota as a Democrat in the U.S. House of Representatives, during which time he served on the House Ways and Means Committee and was a reliable champion for employee benefits issues. Moving to tax reform generally, you were around for EGTRA, which was the Bush 43 era tax cut legislation. And I'm sure over your years in the Ways and Means Committee, there was a lot of idle chatter about comprehensive tax reform. As you mentioned, you came in with representatives Ryan and Brady, who obviously have that on their mind, in your view is successful tax reform legislation defined more by good policy or by good relationships among lawmakers.
